text: The applicant was born in 1961.
The applicant lives in Vanadzor.
The applicant had been granted legal aid.
The applicant was represented by Mr Tumanyan, a lawyer practising in Vanadzor.
The Government were represented by their Agent, Mr G. Kostanyan.
The Government were subsequently represented by Mr Y. Kirakosyan, Representative of the Republic of Armenia to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
On 7 July 2006 the applicant began working as a leading specialist at the Lori Regional Administration.
The applicant held the rank of Civil Servant of the First Category.
From 1 February to 5 March 2008 the applicant took leave.
According to the applicant, he took leave from 1 February to 5 March 2008 in order to be able to participate in the upcoming presidential election to be held in Armenia on 19 February 2008.
The presidential election in Armenia was held on 19 February 2008.
One of the main contenders in the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election was the then Prime Minister, Mr Serzh Sargsyan, representing the ruling party.
One of the main contenders in the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election was the main opposition candidate, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan.
On the day of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, the applicant acted as Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's authorised election assistant (վստահված անձ).

Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against the irregularities which had allegedly occurred in the election process.
Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan announced that the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election had not been free and fair.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The protest rallies held by Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters from 20 February 2008 onwards attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
The main meeting point of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
On 26 February 2008 the applicant took part in a protest rally at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
On 28 February 2008 the applicant took part in a protest rally at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
On 6 March 2008 the Chief of the Lori Regional Police sent a letter to the Lori Regional Governor.
The letter of 6 March 2008 from the Chief of the Lori Regional Police to the Lori Regional Governor stated that the applicant had participated in Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's pre-election campaign.

The letter of 6 March 2008 from the Chief of the Lori Regional Police to the Lori Regional Governor stated that the applicant had participated in unauthorised demonstrations held at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.

The letter of 6 March 2008 from the Chief of the Lori Regional Police to the Lori Regional Governor stated that several other employees of the Lori Regional Administration, who were members of the opposition party, had participated in Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's pre-election campaign.

The letter of 6 March 2008 from the Chief of the Lori Regional Police to the Lori Regional Governor stated that several other employees of the Lori Regional Administration, who were members of the opposition party, had participated in unauthorised demonstrations held at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
On 6 March 2008 the Head of Staff of the Lori Regional Administration asked the applicant to submit a written explanation of his conduct during his leave.

On 6 March 2008 the applicant replied to the Head of Staff of the Lori Regional Administration that he had participated in the peaceful demonstrations held on 26 and 28 February 2008 at Freedom Square in central Yerevan.
The applicant alleged that on 7 March 2008 his house had been searched.
The applicant alleged that after the search of his house on 7 March 2008, he had been taken to a police station and questioned about the demonstrations organised by the opposition.
On 11 March 2008 the applicant was dismissed from his post by an order of the Head of Staff of the Lori Regional Administration.
The order of dismissal of 11 March 2008 was issued with reference to section 33 § 1(j) of the Civil Service Act.
The stated reason for the applicant's dismissal on 11 March 2008 was a breach of the principle of political restraint of civil servants.
On 14 March 2008 the applicant was deprived of the rank of Civil Servant of the First Category.
On 18 April 2008 the applicant instituted proceedings against the Lori Regional Administration, seeking to annul the order of 11 March 2008.

In the proceedings against the Lori Regional Administration, the applicant submitted that from 1 February to 5 March 2008 he had been on leave, during which he had acted as one of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's authorised election assistants.

In the proceedings against the Lori Regional Administration, the applicant submitted that he had participated on two occasions in the opposition demonstrations, which had become the reason for his dismissal.

In the proceedings against the Lori Regional Administration, the applicant argued that he had not used his official position in the interests of any political party since he had been on leave during the relevant period.
In the proceedings against the Lori Regional Administration, the applicant claimed that he was being persecuted for his political views.
On 28 April 2008 the Administrative Court set the case against the Lori Regional Administration down for trial.
On 12 May 2008 the Lori Regional Governor decreed to introduce staffing changes in the Lori Regional Administration by, inter alia, cutting the applicant's post.
On 19 June 2009 the Administrative Court allowed the applicant's claim and annulled the order of 11 March 2008.
On 19 June 2009 the Administrative Court refused to reinstate the applicant in his post.

The Administrative Court found that the conclusion of the Lori Regional Administration that the applicant had breached the principle of political restraint of civil servants by participating in the pre-election campaign and attending the demonstrations had been based on assumptions.

The Administrative Court found that no evidence had been produced to demonstrate that the applicant had engaged in any behaviour that could be characterised as a breach of the principle of political restraint of civil servants.

The Administrative Court found that none of the grounds for dismissal envisaged by section 24 §§ 1-3 of the Civil Service Act were present in the applicant's case and that the dismissal order was to be annulled.

The Administrative Court took into account the fact that the applicant's position at the Lori Regional Administration had been cut on 12 May 2008, bringing to an end the employment relationship between the applicant and the Lori Regional Administration.

The Administrative Court found that it was impossible to restore the employment relationship between the applicant and the Lori Regional Administration and to reinstate the applicant in his previous post.
The Administrative Court awarded the applicant, of its own motion, the sum of his unpaid salary for the period of his involuntary absence, namely from 11 March to 12 May 2008.
The applicant lodged an appeal on points of law against the Administrative Court's judgment of 19 June 2009.
On 9 September 2009 the Court of Cassation declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.
At later dates the applicant addressed letters to various authorities inquiring about the reasons why his post had been cut.

By a letter of 16 December 2010 the applicant was informed by the Lori Regional Governor that two posts, including that of the applicant, had been vacant and had been cut in order to create two other posts within the Lori Regional Administration.

By a letter of 23 February 2011 the applicant was informed by the Deputy Minister of Regional Administration that two posts, including that of the applicant, had been vacant and had been cut in order to create two other posts within the Lori Regional Administration.

Section 24 § 1(d) of the Civil Service Act (in force 2002-2018) provides that a civil servant does not have the right to violate the principle of political restraint of civil servants, that is to use his official position in the interests of political parties or non-governmental organisations, including religious associations, campaign in their favour or carry out other political or religious activities while performing his service duties.

Section 33 § 1(j) of the Civil Service Act (in force 2002-2018) provides that grounds for dismissal of a civil servant from his position include, inter alia, failure to comply with the restrictions envisaged in section 24 §§ 1-3 of that Act.
